message.content:
The largest planet that has been confirmed so far is **HD 100546 b**.  
It orbits the young B-type star HD 100546 at a distance of roughly 50 AU and has:

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Mass | ≈ 20 × Jupiter’s mass (≈ 7 × 10²⁷ kg) |
| Radius | ≈ 1.5 × Jupiter’s radius (≈ 1.0 × 10⁸ m) |

Because it sits near the boundary between massive planets and low‑mass brown dwarfs, its exact classification can vary depending on the criteria used. Nonetheless, it remains the most massive planet that has been reliably detected to date.
